item.case_name: Fact piece about a real thing
item.title: Christmas Eve at Biltmore

turns.text: Make an 8-second widescreen history clip of Biltmore House in Asheville on Christmas Eve 1895, when George Vanderbilt first opened it to family and friends. A slow exterior view is enough. Show 'Biltmore House', 'Asheville, North Carolina' and 'December 24, 1895', plus a small 'Historical reconstruction' label. Warm English narration, historically grounded rather than a fantasy castle.

item.tests: Tests geographic, architectural and period accuracy in a historical reconstruction without misrepresenting generated footage as archival evidence.

answer_sheet.Place and historical event: Biltmore House in Asheville, North Carolina, on December 24, 1895, when George Vanderbilt first opened the house to family and friends.
answer_sheet.Required wording: Biltmore House; Asheville, North Carolina; December 24, 1895; Historical reconstruction.
answer_sheet.Visual treatment: A historically grounded, slow exterior view of the actual house's architecture. Lighting and camera angle are your call.
answer_sheet.People: An exterior view without people is fine; no identifiable portrayal of George Vanderbilt is needed.
answer_sheet.Voice and music: Warm English narration stating the occasion; exact wording, voice and any unobtrusive music are your call.

must_haves: The building is recognizable as Biltmore House, with its pale stone French Renaissance-style facade, steep slate roof and distinctive roofline, rather than a generic castle.
The location and date appear exactly as requested and remain readable.
A legible 'Historical reconstruction' label identifies the imagery as a reconstruction.
No modern cars, contemporary clothing, electric holiday string lights or modern visitor signage appear.
English narration identifies the opening to family and friends, not an opening to the general public.

turns.text: Could you make a history clip of Biltmore House in Asheville on Christmas Eve 1895, when George Vanderbilt first opened it to family and friends? I’ve always found that occasion interesting, and I’d love to get a little sense of it. A slow exterior view is enough, and somewhere in all that I should mention that I want it to be 8 seconds long and widescreen. Please show the words 'Biltmore House', 'Asheville, North Carolina' and 'December 24, 1895', plus a small 'Historical reconstruction' label. I’m a little worried it could end up looking like a fantasy castle, so please keep it historically grounded rather than going in that direction, with warm English narration.

style.prompt: Create a historically grounded documentary reconstruction of the actual Biltmore House, Asheville, North Carolina, on Christmas Eve December 24, 1895. One continuous slow exterior establishing shot, subtle steady forward camera drift, no cuts. Carefully recognizable real architecture: George Vanderbilt's Richard Morris Hunt-designed French Renaissance chateau, long pale Indiana limestone facade, steep slate roofs, authentic dormers, ornate stone details and real building proportions. Show its main entrance facade and forecourt in winter dusk, restrained warm window light, bare deciduous trees, muted natural colors, realistic architectural photography. No fantasy castle, no invented soaring towers, no magical glow, no modern cars or modern fixtures, no exaggerated Christmas decorations, no invented snowfall. Quiet, welcoming period atmosphere. Throughout the shot display four clean readable stable text lines with exact spelling: 'Biltmore House', 'Asheville, North Carolina', 'December 24, 1895'; and a smaller discreet 'Historical reconstruction' label. Keep text clear of the main architecture. Audio: warm, calm English-language narrator clearly says this exact sentence at an unhurried but eight-second-appropriate pace: 'On Christmas Eve, 1895, George Vanderbilt welcomed family and friends to Biltmore House.' No other dialogue. Prioritize authentic building geometry and historical restraint. Landscape widescreen composition, 16:9.
